summary: Every manual rule the instruction keeps has at least one sealed full-report case whose outcome changes when that rule is wrong or reversed. The kept today's steps (projection below three quarters, the above-ceiling counted level, the nought dose) are pinned both by manual-model expectations and by a shipped-package differential that matches the contract. Comparators parse JSON, allow extra top-level/worker keys, and apply the documented dose tolerance and exact TWA/label equality. I found no accepted wrong implementation and no rejected contract-valid one.
checks_performed: Reconciled packet-manifest.json with Glob. All 55 listed files were read. The tests/shipped copies have the same SHA-256 as the environment copies (manifest lines 15-24 vs 52-61), and I read both copies.

tests/expected/limits_workers.jsonl is one 57 KB line, so the Read view stopped at character 40593. That excerpt already held the whole input survey and report rows L000-L165. I recovered the remaining report rows L160-L299 and all 40 group rows with Grep -o, so no range is left unread.

Confirmed with anchored regexes that limits_logs L-1500 holds exactly 1,500 runs and L-PEAKS exactly 500 peaks. This matches the hard assertions at tests/test_outputs.py:343-345, so those assertions cannot reject every submission.

Hand-traced the manual formulas against sealed expectations: reference_duration A1/A4/A7, threshold A1/A2, sampled_time A1/A2/B1/B2, paused_runs A1, partial_surveys A1/A3, whole_shift A1/B1, three_quarters A1/B1/B2, below_three_quarters X1/X2/Y5/Y6/V1/V2, above_ceiling Y1/Z1, rounding R0-R4, status S1-S4/T0-T3/U1, groups G1, quiet_members G1.
For each named rule, derived a plausible wrong implementation and found the sealed case that rejects it (see coverage_sweep).

Checked comparator semantics (tests/test_outputs.py:196-225). Dose uses the midpoint tolerance between the instruction's pass and fail bounds. Sealed doses carry 12 significant digits, a relative error of at most 5e-12, which fits inside the 5e-11 grading bound on both the pass and fail sides. TWA must be exactly equal, and any float produced by nearest-tenth rounding equals the sealed literal. Labels, flags and survey name are compared with exact type and value; extra top-level and worker keys are ignored.

Checked that the differential pairs vary only a field the kept step ignores: shift_minutes for below-3/4 and measured-nothing, and a level above 115 against exactly 115.0 for the ceiling pairs. All 11 pairs are in the domain their family declares.

Checked that relabelling (tests/test_outputs.py:361-380) leaves every manual-defined figure unchanged: dose and sampled time are linear in run minutes, groups are not reordered, and the new ids stay within section 1.
Checked that the driver byte-identity requirement (instruction.md:1) is enforced at tests/test_outputs.py:406-409 and tests/test.sh:23, and that candidate reductions run the verifier's copy.

Checked reachability of the ceiling-to-over rule. One minute counted at 115 dBA already gives a measured dose of 213.3%. Every shift-dose branch (partial, whole, today's below-3/4 step) multiplies by a factor of at least 1, so the TWA is at least 88.3 and the status is over anyway. A ceiling-only 'over' outcome is therefore unreachable within section 1, and the missing isolating case is not a gap.

Checked reachability of the exact-half rounding rule. Worker and group doses lie in Q(2^(1/30)), so no reachable TWA is exactly a half-tenth. The half-up rule cannot change a graded result, and a half-even implementation is not a distinguishable wrong answer.

coverage_sweep.category: Map each required behavior to an assertion that fails if missing or reversed
coverage_sweep.reason: Each test_rule_* function compares the complete report of every survey in its family. Wrong constants 90/5 fail reference_duration. '>' instead of '>=' at 80.0 fails threshold A1. Counted-only sampled time fails sampled_time A1/B1/B2. Counting paused minutes fails paused_runs A1. Projecting to 480 fails partial_surveys A1/A3. '<=' vs '<' at three quarters fails three_quarters A1/B1. The federal TWA fails twa A1/A3. Floor rounding fails rounding R0/R2/R4. Unrounded status fails status T0/T1. A group mean of TWAs fails groups G1. Dropping quiet members fails quiet_members G1. Ceiling '>=' fails ceiling_level A2. Impulse '>' fails impulse A2.

coverage_sweep.category: Check the full core result: values, membership, uniqueness, required outputs
coverage_sweep.reason: compare() checks the survey name, the worker and group row counts, and every README key per row in order. Dose is checked numerically, TWA exactly (or None), and status/ceiling/impulse/id/group by exact type and value. It is not a check of existence or key presence alone.

coverage_sweep.category: Isolating case per named domain rule (not only held-out variation)
coverage_sweep.reason: Every manual clause 1.2-6.1 and each kept today's step has a dedicated family with boundary pairs: 79.9/80.0/80.1, 115.0/115.1, 139.9/140.0, 81.9/82.0 and 85.0/85.1 reported TWAs, exact 3/4 against 457/610, and sampled time below 480 against at least 480 within the below-3/4 family. The ceiling-alone 'over' outcome has no isolating case because it is unreachable (see checks_performed).

Traced 15+ wrong variants. Examples: the shipped package; the manual applied with today's counted-only sampled time in the kept step (below_three_quarters V1 expects 100 vs 200 and V2 211.65 vs 317.48); counting above-ceiling runs at their own level (above_ceiling Y1); projecting below-3/4 surveys to the shift (X1); never projecting below-3/4 surveys (Y6); treating sampled at least the shift as partial (whole_shift A1); group status carrying flags (status H9, measured_nothing G2). Each changes a compared figure.

coverage_sweep.category: Contract-valid alternatives accepted (formatting, ordering, implementation choices)
coverage_sweep.reason: Output formatting comes from the fixed verifier driver, and the report is parsed as JSON. Extra top-level and worker keys are ignored. Int and float numbers are both accepted. The dose tolerance follows instruction.md:5. Any nearest-tenth rounding method yields the same float as the sealed literal. Float summation-order differences under relabelling are about 1e-16 relative and within tolerance. Rejecting ceiling/impulse keys on group rows follows manual 6.1 and the README's group field list.

coverage_sweep.category: Documented restrictions and lifecycle (driver unchanged, figures left to today's code)
coverage_sweep.reason: Driver byte identity is enforced before and after the runs. The kept steps are checked against manual-model expectations and by a differential against the shipped package that tests invariance to the ignored field. That differential is correct under the contract: today's step never reads shift_minutes, and it clamps levels above 115 to 115.

coverage_sweep.category: Proxy behavior, Oracle-specific representation, stale binaries, self-controlled comparisons, unreachable cases
coverage_sweep.reason: Expectations are sealed and pinned in ROSTER, not produced by candidate code. The differential compares the candidate against itself only for invariance and against the shipped copy only for the zero case, and each family also checks absolute values. The sealed inputs are validated against the section 1 limits and the declared trap sets, so no graded case lies outside the contract. The verifier installs its own driver, so no stale candidate driver is graded.

The TWA log term is covered on all three sign partitions: dose below 100 (53.3, 65.9, 73.3), exactly 100 (85.0), and above 100. The zero-dose null TWA is covered. The package has no stateful sequence; runs are summed independent of order, and relabel splitting and shuffling confirm this.

coverage_sweep.category: Section 1 domain extremes reachable and graded
coverage_sweep.reason: 300 workers under 40 codes, a 1,500-run log (confirmed by regex), a 2,880-minute log, 500 peaks (confirmed by regex), shifts of 60 and 1,440 minutes, levels of 40.0 and 140.0, peaks of 60.0 and 170.0, and 12-character ids and 8-character codes are all present and compared in full.

interaction_sweep.case_or_path: sampled_time B1 (100@95, 500@79.9, 60@55.5, shift 720) is partial only when quiet readings count. Expected 229.08; counted-only sampled time gives 1007.9.

rules: 2.2 paused run is not a reading
interaction_sweep.case_or_path: paused_runs A1 has sampled 370/480 and is partial; including paused minutes gives 475 and a different projection factor.
below_three_quarters HC4-0037 V1/V2: today's step fed the manual sampled time (with quiet and paused runs) must give 100 and 211.65, not the counted-only 200 and 317.48.
above_ceiling Y1 (400@90 + 20@118.5, shift 480): clamping to 115 and projecting by 480/420 gives 5178.55. Counting at the own level, or leaving the run out of sampled time, gives different values.
status U1/H9 (TWA 81.0, 140.0 dBC peak): the worker is over and the group is below. measured_nothing A3/G2 is the same with a null TWA.
T0 (unrounded 81.98, reported 82.0) is action. T1 (unrounded 85.03, reported 85.0) is action, not over.
quiet_members G1 in HC4-0028: two quiet members and one at 200% average to 66.67 (TWA 83.2, action). Excluding the zero doses gives 200 (over).
Any reading above 115 dBA forces a shift dose of at least 213.3% on every branch, so status is over from the TWA alone. The interaction cannot change a graded result.

Run splitting, worker shuffling and new ids or names leave doses, sampled times and group rows unchanged. The generated family excludes trap inputs, so no kept-step behavior is exercised under relabelling.
